title: Liquiritin targets NF-kappaB/MAPK signaling to attenuate osteoclastogenesis and triggers apoptosis through PPARgamma activation.
authors: Wu, Jingtao; Zhang, Yuhao; Wang, Yipeng; Liu, Huabin; Sheng, Xiao; Li, Xiongfeng; Lu, Qian; Wang, Yongli
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究甘草苷通过NF-kappaB/MAPK通路抑制破骨细胞生成并诱导凋亡，虽涉及分子对接预测PPARgamma结合，但核心是细胞与动物实验，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Postmenopausal Osteoporosis (PMOP) is an estrogen-deficiency disorder that leads to impaired bone remodeling and a higher incidence of fractures. Liquiritin, a flavonoid from Glycyrrhiza uralensis, has documented bioactivities but previously unexplored potential for PMOP treatment. PURPOSE: To investigate liquiritin's therapeutic effects on PMOP and its underlying mechanisms, constituting the first comprehensive investigation of its role in osteoclasts regulation and apoptosis induction within PMOP pathophysiology. METHODS: Network pharmacology was employed to predict potential targets of Liquiritin in PMOP. The CCK-8 assay assessed its effect on bone marrow-derived macrophages (BMDMs) viability. RANKL was used to induce BMDMs differentiation into mature osteoclasts. TRAcP and F-actin staining detected osteoclasts formation; bone resorption assays evaluated functionality. Western blotting and immunofluorescence were applied to evaluate osteoclasts-related proteins, MAPK/NF-kappaB pathway activity, and apoptosis. Notably, molecular docking predicted Liquiritin's binding to PPARgamma, validated by CETSA. An OVX-induced PMOP mouse model was constructed in vivo; bone microarchitecture and osteoclasts activity were evaluated using micro-CT, H&E, and TRAcP staining. RESULTS: Liquiritin suppressed osteoclasts formation and bone resorption in vitroand mitigated bone loss in vivo by downregulating osteoclasts-specific genes, inhibiting MAPK/NF-kappaB pathways, and most importantly, inducing PPARgamma-mediated apoptosis-a novel mechanistic insight not previously reported. CONCLUSION: Liquiritin exerts anti-osteoporotic effects by targeting Osteoclastogenesis, inducing apoptosis, and inhibiting bone resorption via PPARgamma activation, highlighting its novel therapeutic potential for PMOP treatment.
abstract_zh: 背景：绝经后骨质疏松症（PMOP）是一种雌激素缺乏性疾病，导致骨重塑受损和骨折发生率升高。甘草苷（Liquiritin）是甘草（Glycyrrhiza uralensis）中的一种黄酮类化合物，已有文献记载其生物活性，但其在PMOP治疗中的潜力此前未被探索。目的：研究甘草苷对PMOP的治疗效果及其潜在机制，这是首次对其在PMOP病理生理中破骨细胞调控和凋亡诱导作用进行的全面研究。方法：采用网络药理学预测甘草苷在PMOP中的潜在靶点。CCK-8实验评估其对骨髓来源巨噬细胞（BMDMs）活力的影响。使用RANKL诱导BMDMs分化为成熟破骨细胞。TRAcP和F-actin染色检测破骨细胞形成；骨吸收实验评估其功能。应用Western blotting和免疫荧光评估破骨细胞相关蛋白、MAPK/NF-kappaB通路活性及凋亡。值得注意的是，分子对接预测甘草苷与PPARgamma的结合，并通过CETSA验证。在体内构建OVX诱导的PMOP小鼠模型；使用micro-CT、H&E和TRAcP染色评估骨微结构和破骨细胞活性。结果：甘草苷在体外抑制破骨细胞形成和骨吸收，并在体内减轻骨丢失，其机制为下调破骨细胞特异性基因、抑制MAPK/NF-kappaB通路，以及最重要的是，诱导PPARgamma介导的凋亡——这是一种此前未报道的新机制见解。结论：甘草苷通过靶向破骨细胞生成、诱导凋亡及通过PPARgamma激活抑制骨吸收发挥抗骨质疏松作用，凸显其在PMOP治疗中的新型治疗潜力。
